key_insight: BrainLM and BrainHarmonix did not demonstrate a clear predictive advantage over simple baselines on PreventAD, highlighting gaps in fMRI foundation-model transfer.
clinical_relevance: These findings do not establish reliable prediction of mild cognitive impairment progression or β-amyloid burden in adults with a family history of Alzheimer’s disease.
method: Evaluated frozen and fine-tuned foundation-model features against functional connectivity and a majority-class dummy classifier.
Tested sex, age group, progression to mild cognitive impairment, and β-amyloid burden.
Adapted released code, preprocessing, and normalization to enable evaluation.
evidence_signal: The study included 343 quality-controlled participants, 218 with amyloid PET; neither clinical target exceeded dummy-classifier accuracy, and AUC remained near chance.
watch_item: Substantial code changes and unclear preprocessing requirements limited streamlined independent use of both models.
paper_title: Current gaps in downstream applications of fMRI foundation models: lessons learned from BrainLM & BrainHarmonix on Prevent-AD
